papers.title: Strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with nuclear dimension one and infinite decomposition rank
papers.abstract: We construct the first, to our knowledge, examples of strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with finite nuclear dimension and infinite decomposition rank. The examples are extensions of the form $0\to I \to E\to C(\mathbb{T})\to 0$ where $I$ is a simple AF-algebra. These examples are in some sense the easiest `natural' choices in light of Spielberg's work on AF-embedding extensions and the behavior of each dimension theory with respect to extensions. The standard extension bound provides $\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}} E \leq 2$ which is improved to 1 by recent work of Evington, Faurot and Schafhauser. Nuclear dimension 1 is the lowest possible for such an example because decomposition rank and nuclear dimension agree at 0. Finally, failure of the comparison property used to show infinite decomposition rank was inspired by local operator space techniques of Junge, Ozawa and Ruan.

papers.title: On the Equivalence of Linear and $C^*$ Extremality for Unital Completely Positive Maps on Commutative Real $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital commutative real $C^*$-algebra and $\mathcal H$ be a finite dimensional real Hilbert space. In this article, an easily verifiable necessary and sufficient condition for a linear extreme unital completely positive (UCP) map $\Phi:\mathcal A \rightarrow B(\mathcal H)$ to be C*-extreme, is obtained. As an application, the $C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A$ on which linear extreme UCP maps coincide with the $C^*$-extreme ones, are classified.

papers.title: Cleanness and real rank zero in $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: A unital $C^*$-algebra is called clean if every element is the sum of an idempotent and an invertible element. We prove that cleanness is equivalent to real rank zero. More precisely, the invertible summand can be chosen with inverse norm at most $2+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and the constant $2$ is optimal. In particular, every von Neumann algebra is clean, answering a question of Lam. Clean decompositions with uniformly bounded idempotent summands characterize real rank zero and stable rank one. Moreover, $*$-cleanness, defined by requiring the idempotent summands to be projections, is equivalent to real rank zero, stable rank one, and triviality of the $K_1$-group. Finally, sharp cleanness, defined by requiring clean decompositions with inverse norm at most $2$, is equivalent to real rank zero and the $SAW^*$ property.

papers.title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted étale groupoid model
papers.abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal \'etale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Almost unimodular quantum groups
papers.abstract: We define a locally compact quantum group $\mathbb{G}$ to be almost unimodular if its modular element is diagonalizable. This is shown to be equivalent to the almost periodicity of a novel weight on the dual von Neumann algebra, which we call the middle Haar weight. The point modular spectrum of this weight is related to the point spectrum of $\delta$, and we prove that unimodularity of $\mathbb{G}$ is equivalent to traciality of this weight. When $\delta$ is affiliated with the center of $L^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, we show that there is a canonical closed, normal, unimodular quantum subgroup $\mathbb{G}_1 \leq \mathbb{G}$ which assumes the role of the unimodular part of $\mathbb{G}$, and moreover the openness of this quantum subgroup is equivalent to the almost periodicity of $\mathbb{G}$. Additionally, we establish several permanence properties of almost unimodularity.

papers.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
papers.abstract: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.

papers.title: $C^*$-selflessness for free Burnside groups
papers.abstract: The free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is obtained from the free group of rank $m$ by imposing the relations $w^n=1$ for all words $w$. We prove that $B(m,n)$ is completely $C^*$-selfless for every $m\geq2$ and every odd exponent $n\geq557$. Consequently, its reduced group $C^*$-algebra has stable rank one and strict comparison of positive elements by its canonical trace. This answers the question of whether $C^*$-selfless groups can satisfy a nontrivial group law. The proof establishes Ozawa's property $P_{PHP}$ by combining a combinatorial construction with a relative power-avoidance argument based on the canonical forms of Atkarskaya-Rips-Tent.

papers.title: On JT boundary algebras
papers.abstract: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.

papers.title: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger. While for classical graphs the values of the minimum generalised cut and the minimum ordinary cut coincide---recovering the classical max-flow min-cut theorem---we also show how it is more natural to think of flows as duals of generalised cuts instead of ordinary cuts.

papers.title: Quasicentral modulus for almost normal operators
papers.abstract: In 1984, Voiculescu conjectured that the Hilbert--Schmidt quasicentral modulus vanishes for every almost normal operator. We prove this conjecture.
